Owner decision 2026-11-23: brotli4j (com.aayushatharva.brotli4j, a JNI binding) is not ported; Brotli runs on the BCL System.IO.Compression.BrotliEncoder/BrotliDecoder structs, available since .NET Core 2.1. DecoderJNI.Wrapper is the BCL System.IO.Compression.BrotliDecoder struct (written with its namespace because the class has the same simple name). brotli4j's DecoderJNI.Wrapper keeps an input buffer that push(length) decodes, keeps the decoded output inside the native decoder until pull() takes it (pull(maxBytes) and the maxOutputChunkSize constructor bound one pull), and reports ERROR, DONE, NEEDS_MORE_INPUT, NEEDS_MORE_OUTPUT or OK; decoder_jni.cc reports ERROR when the stream ends before the pushed input does ("Bytes after stream end are not allowed"). The BCL decoder has one call, Decompress(source, destination, out bytesConsumed, out bytesWritten), which decodes input and writes output into the caller's span in the same step and returns an OperationStatus (Done, DestinationTooSmall, NeedMoreData, InvalidData). The class keeps the wrapper state in CLR fields: inputBuffer with inputOffset/inputLength (getInputBuffer() and the unconsumed pushed input), outputBuffer with outputLength (the output pull() would take; at most min(size, 64 KiB) bytes per call, MAX_OUTPUT_BUFFER_SIZE, so a large size does not allocate an array of that size; pull(size) also returns less when less is available) and lastStatus. Two CLR-only private methods stand for the wrapper calls: Push(length) runs one Decompress call over the unconsumed input into the emptied outputBuffer (NeedMoreData with a full outputBuffer becomes DestinationTooSmall, because the decoder may still hold output), and Pull(), called after the output was copied, releases it and continues decoding after DestinationTooSmall. Status mapping: InvalidData is ERROR, Done is DONE once the output was taken (the finishing call may write its last output at once) and ERROR when pushed input is left (the decoder_jni.cc check), NeedMoreData is NEEDS_MORE_INPUT, DestinationTooSmall is NEEDS_MORE_OUTPUT, and OK (brotli4j's status after a pull with pushed input left) does not occur because Pull continues at once. hasOutput() is outputLength != 0. The BCL decoder is a mutable struct without a constructor that creates its native state lazily on the first Decompress call, so the field is not readonly and destroy() is Dispose(). The static initializer (Brotli.ensureAvailability() wrapped in ExceptionInInitializerError) is a static constructor calling Brotli.EnsureAvailability(), which never throws; an exception thrown by a static constructor reaches callers as TypeInitializationException, so the try/catch is not repeated. readBytes(ByteBuf, ByteBuffer) copies into the byte[] inputBuffer from index 0 (ReadBytes into a span of the first limit bytes; the Buffer port has no ReadBytes(byte[], int, int)). A scratch console probe (not in the repository) checked the port with input buffer sizes 1 to 1 MiB, output sizes 1 to int.MaxValue, input fed byte by byte or at once, random and compressible data, trailing bytes inside and after the pushed input, corrupt and truncated streams. The decompress() switch over decoder.getStatus() is a switch over lastStatus with the same branches (DONE forwards output first; no OK branch); forwardOutput copies outputBuffer into accumBuffer (keeping the comment that the content must be copied) and then calls Pull. new DecoderJNI.Wrapper(inputBufferSize) in handlerAdded creates the decoder and the two buffers. List<Object> out is IList<object> @out, in is @in; checkPositive/checkPositiveOrZero are the Common ObjectUtil methods; catch (Exception e) { ...; throw e; } is throw;.

BrotliEncoderChannel is the BCL System.IO.Compression.BrotliEncoder struct (written with its namespace because the class has the same simple name; a mutable struct, so the field is not readonly). Encoder.Parameters is BrotliOptions: BrotliEncoder(Encoder.Parameters parameters, boolean isSharable) is BrotliEncoder(BrotliOptions parameters, bool isSharable), keeping the Java parameter name and Javadoc, so that a non-sharable encoder can still be created; BrotliEncoder(Encoder.Parameters) is not ported (with the type mapped it would be BrotliEncoder(BrotliOptions), which exists; its Javadoc is recorded as library-not-ported), and BrotliEncoder(BrotliOptions) calls the two-argument constructor directly. new BrotliEncoderChannel(this, parameters) is new BrotliEncoder(quality, window); the mode is not passed (see BrotliMode). brotliEncoderChannel.write(nioBuffer) is Compress(source, outputBuffer, ..., isFinalBlock: false), flush() is Flush(outputBuffer, ...), and close() is Compress(empty, outputBuffer, ..., isFinalBlock: true) followed by Dispose() in a finally block, as brotli4j's Encoder.close() runs encode(FINISH) and destroys the native encoder; each is repeated while it returns DestinationTooSmall and InvalidData throws IOException("encoding failed") as brotli4j does. Every compressed chunk goes through Writer.write, as brotli4j's pushOutput hands its output to the destination channel; outputBuffer is 16384 bytes, the intermediate buffer size of brotli4j's BrotliEncoderChannel. WritableByteChannel has no BCL counterpart: Writer keeps write/isOpen/close without the interface, ByteBuffer is ReadOnlySpan<byte>, and the position of the borrowed nio buffer is the consumed byte count (CompressionUtil.SafeReadableNioBuffer returns ReadOnlyMemory<byte>). ClosedChannelException is the Transport one. ChannelFuture/ChannelPromise are Task/TaskCompletionSource: ctx.newPromise() is a TaskCompletionSource, setFailure is SetException, ctx.newSucceededFuture() is Task.CompletedTask, ctx.writeAndFlush(buf, promise) copies the outcome of WriteAndFlushAsync into the promise with TrySetFromTask, and close(ctx, promise) is CloseAsync(ctx, cancellationToken) returning EncoderUtil.CloseAfterFinishEncode (docs/transport-porting.md, docs/common-task-composition.md). The anonymous Runnable is a lambda passed to Executor.Execute. @ChannelHandler.Sharable is [Sharable] and isSharable() is the Transport port's IsSharable property (as codec-base DatagramPacketDecoder overrides it). AttributeKey/attr are the Common AttributeKey<T>/IAttribute<T> (as codec-mqtt MqttCodecUtil). The Writer fields the enclosing class reads (writableBuffer, closeFuture) and its constructor are internal. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException; checkNotNull's NullPointerException is ArgumentNullException; catch (Exception e) { ...; throw e; } is throw;. A scratch probe (not in the repository) checked four quality/window/mode combinations, sharable and non-sharable instances, one instance shared by two channels and that every flushed message decodes at once.

The public parameters() accessor only returns the brotli4j type and is not ported (it has no comment). The package-private constructor BrotliOptions(Encoder.Parameters) is the internal constructor BrotliOptions(int quality, int window, BrotliMode mode); StandardCompressionOptions.brotli(quality, window, mode) calls it with the values it validated, as it calls setQuality/setWindow/setMode(mode.adapt()) in Java. The Brotli.isAvailable() check and its IllegalStateException (InvalidOperationException) are kept and never fire. DEFAULT is quality 4, window 22, TEXT: new Encoder.Parameters().setQuality(4).setMode(TEXT) leaves lgwin at -1, which brotli4j does not pass to the native encoder (encoder_jni.cc sets BROTLI_PARAM_LGWIN only when lgwin >= 0), so brotli uses BROTLI_DEFAULT_WINDOW 22; the BCL constructor takes the window explicitly ("The minimum value is 10, and the maximum value is 24").

Owner decision 2026-11-23: java.util.zip.Checksum is System.IO.Hashing.NonCryptographicHashAlgorithm (package 11.0.0), so ByteBufChecksum is an internal abstract class deriving from it and can be passed wherever a NonCryptographicHashAlgorithm is expected. The Checksum members keep the Java call shape: update(int) is Update(int), update(byte[], int, int) is Update(byte[], int, int), getValue() is GetValue() returning the Java long, and reset() is the base class's public abstract Reset(). The base class constructor takes the hash length, so the constructor is ByteBufChecksum(int hashLengthInBytes); its abstract GetCurrentHashCore(Span<byte>) is implemented by the subclasses. Append(ReadOnlySpan<byte>), abstract in the base class, is Checksum's default update(ByteBuffer): it copies at most 4096 bytes at a time into a temporary array and calls Update(b, 0, length), the branch the Java default takes for a buffer without an accessible array. wrapChecksum(Checksum) is internal static WrapChecksum(NonCryptographicHashAlgorithm) and returns a ByteBufChecksum unchanged. The anonymous ByteProcessor is a Func<byte, bool> created in the constructor (a field initializer cannot reference this). The Buffer port has no hasArray()/array()/arrayOffset(): update(ByteBuf, int, int) reads the range with AsReadOnlySequence and takes the array branch when it is one segment backed by a managed array (MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray, docs/buffer-porting.md, Array extraction; the array index is arrayOffset() + off), otherwise it visits the bytes with ForEachByte. The private JdkByteBufChecksum keeps its name and wraps any NonCryptographicHashAlgorithm: update(int) appends the low eight bits as a one-byte span, update(byte[], int, int) appends the array range, the CRC32/Adler32 branches of update(ByteBuf, int, int) append the span of CompressionUtil.SafeNioBuffer to System.IO.Hashing.Crc32/Adler32, and getSafeBuffer drops the Java 22-24 copy into scratchBuffer (a JVM-only work-around; the comment linking the JDK issue is kept). getValue() reads GetCurrentHashAsUInt32() for System.IO.Hashing.Crc32, Adler32 and XxHash32 (the unsigned 32-bit value that CRC32/Adler32.getValue() return); any other NonCryptographicHashAlgorithm can be wrapped, updated and reset but GetValue() throws NotSupportedException, because the base class exposes the hash only as bytes in a byte order each type defines. The wrapper reports the wrapped HashLengthInBytes and writes the wrapped GetCurrentHash bytes (Crc32 little endian, XxHash32 and Adler32 big endian). Crc32 is written System.IO.Hashing.Crc32 because the bzip2 Crc32 of this module shares the namespace. Unsigned bytes from ForEachByte give the same checksum as the signed Java bytes, because update(int) uses only the low eight bits.

The package-private class is internal and the field in is @in. readUnsignedByte() is the Buffer port's ReadByte(), which returns the unsigned octet (docs/buffer-porting.md, "Raw integer access and CLR octets"); readUnsignedShort()/readUnsignedInt() return ushort/uint, which widen to the long readData with zero extension as the Java int/long results do. refill() keeps the octet in a byte local (Java: an int holding 0..255) because or-ing an int into the long raises CS0675 ("Bitwise-or operator used on a sign-extended operand"); the value is the same. Java int/long arithmetic that wraps is unchecked in C# too (the projects are unchecked) and >>> is C# >>>. The (int) narrowing of the long keeps the low 32 bits. review.scope: Owner decision 2026-11-23: the solution stays on .NET 10 and java.util.zip.Inflater is the internal CLR stand-in Inflater (Inflater.cs, listed with this entry; it has no Java file and no entry of its own). It keeps the Java call shape (setInput, inflate, needsInput, finished, getRemaining, getTotalOut, needsDictionary, setDictionary, reset, end) and reads a raw DeflateStream (nowrap) or a ZLibStream in decompression mode from a private feed stream that SetInput fills. DeflateStream reads its source only when its zlib stream needs input, into an 8192-byte buffer, so fed whole buffers it reads past the end of the deflate data and getRemaining() is unknown after the end; fed one byte per Read, it takes exactly the deflate data (DeflateStream.ReadCore of .NET 10.0.8 and SP\zlibprobe on this host). Owner decision: the GZIP wrapper, whose header and trailer Netty parses itself while it inflates the body raw, feeds one byte per Read (new Inflater(true, true)), so getRemaining() is exact at the end of each member and the trailer is read at the right offset; ZLIB, NONE and ZLIB_OR_NONE feed whole buffers, where the bytes after the end are not used. Measured through the stand-in (scratch probe, 8 MB of output): whole buffers about 290-360 MB/s, one byte per Read about 28-31 MB/s (the owner's measurement with SP\zlibprobe: 381 and 21 MB/s), so GZIP decoding is roughly ten times slower than ZLIB/NONE decoding. inflate(b, off, len) reads until len bytes are produced or a Read returns 0, as zlib's inflate() fills the output from the available input; a Read that returns 0 after an empty source read means more input is needed, one without a source read means the end (finished()). When the output was filled, the stand-in reads one byte ahead to learn whether the end was reached in the same call, as Java reports through finished() (zlib decodes the end-of-block code and the trailer without output space); the byte is returned by the next inflate(). DataFormatException is the InvalidDataException the BCL streams throw for corrupt data. Preset dictionaries: the BCL streams have no dictionary API and report zlib's Z_NEED_DICT as an unexpected ZLibException, so the feed hands the two zlib header bytes to the ZLibStream on their own and checks the RFC 1950 FDICT flag of a valid header; needsDictionary() becomes true once the header is seen (zlib first reads the four DICTID bytes too) and setDictionary throws NotSupportedException. The "System.IO.Compression.UseStrictValidation" AppContext switch (off by default) makes DeflateStream throw InvalidDataException when its source returns 0 before the end; the stand-in treats that exception, thrown right after an empty feed read, as "needs input" (a scratch probe passed with the switch on and off). reset() creates a new BCL stream; end() disposes it. Preset dictionaries: with no dictionary configured, a stream with the zlib FDICT flag still fails with Netty's DecompressionException; with one configured, Inflater.SetDictionary throws NotSupportedException (the BCL streams have no dictionary API), and the constructors/builder methods that take a dictionary stay as public Java API and document this.
